properties.Religious Significance: Believed to be the spot where Lord Rama bathed during his 14-year exile; most sacred ghat in Nashik
properties.Key Rituals: Holy dip, asthi visarjan (ash immersion), pitru tarpan
properties.Built / Restored By: Built 1696 CE by Chitrarao Khatarkar; restored by Gopikabai (mother of Peshwa Madhavrao)
properties.Nearby Temples: Kapaleshwar Mahadev, Naroshankar (bell), Kalaram Temple, Godavari Mata Mandir
properties.Accessibility: Auto-rickshaw / bus to Panchavati; ~15 min from city centre
properties.Notes: Bones reputedly dissolve in water; Godavari temple opens only during Kumbh Mela

properties.Religious Significance: Built by Ahilyabai Holkar; Godavari locally called 'Ganga'; spot where river turns 90 deg
properties.Key Rituals: Evening aarti, prayer, meditation, holy dip
properties.Nearby Temples: Multiple shrines to various Hindu deities along the ghat
properties.Accessibility: Auto-rickshaw to 'Ganga Ghat, Ramkund, Panchavati'; 15-20 min from city centre
properties.Notes: Lamp-lit evening aarti draws large crowds; similar to Varanasi Ganga aarti

properties.Religious Significance: Sacred area where Rama, Sita and Lakshmana lived during exile; Aranya Kanda of Ramayana set here
properties.Nearby Temples: Kalaram Temple, Sita Gufa, Ardhanareshwar, Goraram, Hanuman, Neelkantheshwar, Balaji
properties.Accessibility: Local bus to Panchavati or auto from city
properties.Notes: Five sacred banyan trees (panch + vati) still present; Triveni Sangam (confluence of 3 rivers) nearby
Often visited alongside Ramkund and Lakshmankund as a trio

properties.Religious Significance: Associated with Lakshmana; part of the Ramkund-Sitakund-Lakshmankund sacred cluster
properties.Notes: Maintenance has been noted as inadequate in visitor reports

properties.Religious Significance: Symbolic source of Godavari; sacred bathing site for Shaiva Akharas during Kumbh Mela; beside one of India's 12 Jyotirlinga temples
properties.Key Rituals: Shahi Snan (royal dip) during Kumbh, daily ritual baths
properties.Notes: Brahmagiri Mountain - official source of Godavari at elevation 920 m

properties.Religious Significance: Scenic ghat along Godavari upstream, near Gangapur Dam area; popular nature & picnic spot
properties.Accessibility: Auto-rickshaw / cab ~20 min from city centre
properties.Notes: Someshwar Waterfall nearby; Gangapur Dam is a key water source

properties.Religious Significance: Named after Maratha queen Ahilyabai Holkar who built/patronised Ganga Ghat and many temples along Godavari
properties.Notes: Often grouped with Ganga Ghat in references; historical patronage of Maratha era

properties.Religious Significance: Designated site for immersion of ashes (asthi) of deceased; belief that bones dissolve in waters
properties.Key Rituals: Asthi visarjan (ash & bone immersion), pitru tarpan, shraddha
properties.Notes: Also used for immersing floral offerings post-puja

properties.Religious Significance: Sacred confluence of three rivers; highly auspicious in Hindu tradition for pitru karma and bathing
properties.Notes: Considered extremely auspicious; one of three major Triveni Sangams in Maharashtra
